item.title: TGH to open Innovation Center in Ybor City
item.description: Tampa General Hospital will celebrate the grand opening of its new Innovation Center on Wednesday on the eastern edge of Ybor City — a milestone moment for the hospital that comes as it celebrates its annual Innovation Week. item.title: Sarasota family office acquires large manufacturing plant
item.description: Nickolas Asset Management, a Sarasota-based family office owned by Nickolas Reinhart, has acquired a manufacturing plant. The 120,000-square-foot facility was owned by Material Difference Technologies, a plastic resin supplier and processor headquartered in Bradenton. item.title: Naples home sells for $16.5M, full asking price
item.description: A custom-built home in Collier County sold for $16.5 million in late 2025 — a price the builder says was the most expensive home sale in Naples in December 2025.The house, 2426 Indian Pipe Way, is in Grey Oaks Country Club, west of Interstate 75 and north of downtown Naples. item.title: Hillsborough College secures $1.54M in funding for AI center
item.description: Hillsborough College has secured multiple federal grants to establish an Artificial Intelligence Innovation Center to provide workforce-ready training for students across Tampa Bay. The college secured a $1.29 million grant from the U.S. Department of Education in January, and on Monday announced it’s AI initiative was awarded another $250,000 in community project funding. item.title: Tampa Bay Rays launch streaming service to broadcast 2026 games
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays have launched a streaming service to air their games on TV this upcoming season.The team announced this week the creation of Rays.TV to broadcast every game except those scheduled to be nationally televised.The full season subscription for the platform is $99.99, with season ticket holders getting a 50% discount. item.description: Sarasota County is primed to buy one of the most notable properties in the region, a colorful gateway to Siesta Key that includes bay frontage, docks, water sports outposts and even a restaurant, in a $18.1 million deal. item.title: High-tech Israeli medical firm opens Manatee facility, plans 100 jobs
item.description: A fast-growing medtech firm based in Israel recently celebrated the opening of its new U.S. headquarters in north Manatee County. The group of officials and business leaders at the opening event, held Feb. 2, included Florida Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. The firm, Ossio, makes metal-free fixation implants out of a proprietary material that allows for bone regeneration.
